restrictions: Two-block messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' of 128 bytes each, standard IV, standard padding (shared third block), rounds 0..30 in every compression, full feed-forward and full 256-bit digest.
Algorithm is the published Li-Liu-Wang EUROCRYPT 2024 (ePrint 2024/349, Sect. 4.2) 31-step SHA-256 collision attack with one starting point (l = 48); the cryptanalysis is attributed, not original.
Phase 2 runs exactly N = 2^50.3 independent uniform first blocks and processes at most 64 table matches; every returned pair is re-verified on the complete padded target.

time_log2 charges the starting-point search (budget 2^40), exhaustive (W7,W8) enumeration, 2^48 table entries, all 2^50.3 trials with a 2048-word-operation surcharge each, Phase-3 budgets and verification at v5 prices (C = 2140).
success_probability 0.6 is a heuristic lower bound resting on declared heuristics H-table, H-match and H-step3; the paper's estimate is about 0.865 for this N.
The certificate is the published ASIACRYPT 2024 practical pair, included only as exact-target witness evidence; the algorithm never reads it and it is not nonuniform advice.

heuristics.statement: A single starting point yields about 2^48 valid solutions of (A_i)_{-3..12}, (E_i)_{1..12}, (W_i)_{5..12}: 2^14 admissible W5, 2^23 admissible W6, and about 2^11 (W7,W8) pairs satisfying the (E_3,E_4) conditions.
heuristics.scope: The EUROCRYPT 2024 31-step characteristic with message differences in W5..W9, W16, W18, for one SAT-generated starting point.
heuristics.extrapolation: The 2^11 count is the paper's experimental enumeration for one starting point and is assumed representative for the starting point found in Phase 0.
heuristics.limitations: Not proved; a smaller table of 2^(48-d) entries leaves the time bound unchanged but lowers success; the declared 0.6 holds for d <= 1.1.

heuristics.statement: For independent uniform first blocks, the 96-bit word triple (A_-1, A_-2, A_-3) of the 31-round chaining value hits the fixed 2^48-entry key set with probability about 2^-48 per trial, independently across trials.
heuristics.scope: Single 31-round SHA-256 compression from the standard IV, restricted to three output words, against a fixed key set built independently of the trials.
heuristics.extrapolation: Standard random-function behaviour of one compression on independent inputs; no full-scale run of 2^50.3 trials has been performed by this submission.
heuristics.limitations: Unproved random-function heuristic; the certificate shows a standard-IV match is reachable but is a single instance.

heuristics.statement: After a match, the free words W13, W14, W15 satisfy the remaining conditions on E_13, E_14, E_15, W16 and W18 with probability about 2^-1.3, each attempt costing well below 2^36 target-compression units.
heuristics.scope: Phase 3 of the EUROCRYPT 2024 attack on 31-step SHA-256.
heuristics.extrapolation: gamma ~ 1.3 was measured by the authors with 100 tests; the success bound tolerates gamma up to about 2.42.
heuristics.limitations: Small published sample; per-attempt cost is a generous budget, not a measured value.

heuristics.statement: One starting point satisfying all differential conditions on rounds 5..12 can be found with the SAT/SMT model within 2^40 target-compression units.
heuristics.extrapolation: The paper reports about 2^31.7 for this step; the budget adds a large margin.
heuristics.limitations: SAT solver running time is empirical; even a much larger value up to about 2^50 would not change the declared scalar.
